about: The evangelium of the formulary “2nd Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time, Jesus told this parable to the Pharisees: A certain man held a great supper and invited many. And at the hour of the supper he sent his servant to tell the invited guests to come, because all is now ready. And all of them together began to make excuses. The first said to him: I bought a farm, and I have need to go out and see it; I beg you, hold me excused. And a second said: I bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to test them; I beg you, hold me excused. And another said: I have taken a wife, and for that reason I cannot come. And on his return the servant told his master these things. Then the householder, in anger, said to his servant: Go out quickly into the squares and streets of the city, and bring the poor and the infirm and the blind and the lame in here. And the servant said: Master, it has been done as you commanded, and there is still room. And the master said to the servant: Go out into the roads and hedges, and compel them to enter, so that my house may be filled. But I say to you that none of those men who were invited will taste my supper.
